Real division by n; n = 0 gives the junk value 0, and a pairwise coprime infinite set may contain 0 only if it is {0, 1}, which is finite, so 0 never occurs under the hypotheses.

review.words: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is $$ \sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1} $$ irrational?

statement.text:
import Mathlib
import Nodes.«variant-c91009b9».Context

/-- Erdős 257 for pairwise coprime `A` with convergent `∑_{n ∈ A} 1/n`. Known: P. Erdős,
*On the irrationality of certain series*, Math. Student 36 (1968), 222–226, Theorem (p. 222:
"Let `(n_i, n_j) = 1`, `∑ 1/n_i < ∞`. Then `∑ 1/(t^{n_i} - 1)` is irrational for every
`t ≥ 2`"; here `t = 2`). Erdős adds that coprimality can be dropped by "more complicated
arguments" whose details he does not give. The primes are pairwise coprime but `∑ 1/p`
diverges, so they are not a case of this statement. -/
theorem Opn.erdos_257_coprime_summable :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime →
      Summable (fun n : A => (1 : ℝ) / n.1) →
      Irrational (∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1)) := by
  sorry

witness.text:
import Mathlib

theorem witness : ∃ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite ∧ A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧
    Summable fun (n : A) => (1 : ℝ) / (n.1 : ℝ) := by
  refine ⟨(fun p => p ^ 2) '' {p : ℕ | p.Prime}, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact Set.Infinite.image (fun x _ y _ h => Nat.pow_left_injective (by norm_num) h)
      Nat.infinite_setOf_prime
  · rintro _ ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩ _ ⟨q, hq, rfl⟩ hne
    have hpq : p ≠ q := fun h => hne (by rw [h])
    exact Nat.Coprime.pow 2 2 ((Nat.coprime_primes hp hq).2 hpq)
  · have hs : Summable (fun m : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / (m : ℝ) ^ 2) :=
      Real.summable_one_div_nat_pow.2 (by norm_num)
    have hinj : Function.Injective
        (fun n : ((fun p => p ^ 2) '' {p : ℕ | p.Prime}) => Nat.sqrt n.1) := by
      rintro ⟨_, p, hp, rfl⟩ ⟨_, q, hq, rfl⟩ h
      simp only [Nat.sqrt_eq'] at h
      subst h
      rfl
    refine (hs.comp_injective hinj).congr ?_
    rintro ⟨_, p, hp, rfl⟩
    simp [Nat.sqrt_eq']
